title: std/ESP-IDF foundation + ESPHome-native plant monitor
description: Foundation plus first product. Pivot the M5StickC Plus firmware from no_std esp-hal to std on ESP-IDF (esp-idf-svc, esp-idf-hal, esp-idf-sys), then ship a soil-moisture plant monitor that appears to Home Assistant as a native ESPHome device (protobuf over TCP 6053 plus mDNS) so HA stores, graphs and alerts on the readings. Board is ESP32-PICO-D4 (4MB flash, 520KB SRAM, no PSRAM), which runs std comfortably. Why std: it turns the ESPHome native API into a roughly one-week job instead of weeks (std::net TCP, prost protobuf, ESP-IDF WiFi/mDNS/OTA, pure-Rust Noise) and it also simplifies OTA. Domain crates (led-core, plant-core, the esphome-api protocol core) stay pure and framework-free. Architecture: hexagonal/ECB plus Functional Core / Imperative Shell (Bernhardt Boundaries) plus dogfooding the ~/code/tools contract suite (hex-lint, effect-audit, cargo-regime-check) as the CI gates that enforce both. This epic reverses and supersedes the no_std OTA epic stick-c-plus-qqh (ESP-IDF supplies WiFi/OTA/mDNS natively). MVP milestone is the plaintext native-API sensor entity graphing in HA. Full design saved at docs/plans/plant-monitor-esphome-native-api.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] MVP: Soil Moisture graphs in HA History and a watering alert fires (qhw.22 closed)
- [ ] the native-API framework is generic: fmz adds a Light entity without rewriting (fmz.2 lands on it cleanly)
- [ ] architecture gates green and proven fail-able: hex-lint, effect-audit --require-domain, cargo-regime-check

HA stood up on the LAN, Ansible-managed (infra repo). Status + decisions:

DECISION (AC #3) — HA **Container** (Podman Quadlet, `Network=host`) on **fedora**, Ansible-managed. NOT HAOS-in-a-VM. Why: the homelab is already Ansible/Podman-Quadlet driven and fedora is the LAN box on the device's L2; host networking gives native mDNS + the ESPHome native-API (:6053) path on the same L2 with zero extra infra. HAOS-in-a-VM can't be a fleet service and adds a VM to babysit. No MQTT (native-API path). No ESPHome dashboard (the Rust firmware doesn't use it).

WHERE — new `lan_quadlet` Ansible role (host-net sibling of the tailnet-sidecar `service_quadlet` fleet). Registry: `host_vars/fedora.yml::fedora_lan_services.home-assistant`. HA 2026.7.1 pinned by digest, amd64. Deploy: `just home-assistant`. Full doc: infra `docs/home-assistant.md`.

REACHABLE (AC #1, host on same L2) —
  - LAN:    http://10.0.0.10:8123   (fedora; HA is host-networked on 10.0.0.0/24)
  - tailnet: http://fedora.mist-walleye.ts.net:8123
  - .homelab: https://homeassistant.homelab (via oracle-arm Caddy gateway; HA's own auth, no oauth2-proxy)

mDNS BROWSE WORKS (AC #2) — `avahi-browse -at` from the HA host shows HA's own advert:
    `+ wlp3s0 IPv4 Home   _home-assistant._tcp   local`
  proving zeroconf/mDNS is live on fedora's L2. When the device advertises `_esphomelib._tcp` it'll be visible the same way.

RECORDER — on by default (`default_config:`), default 10-day retention kept (not shortened, per qhw.22 needs). Stores history once onboarded.

REMAINING — onboarding (create the owner account) is a manual browser step (owner identity/password — can't be Ansible'd). Open https://homeassistant.homelab or http://10.0.0.10:8123 and complete it. Recorder then stores history and this bead's ACs are fully met.

FOR qhw.22 (adopt) — device at 10.0.0.11 (DHCP, MAC DE:AD:BE:EF:00:01); a DHCP reservation for that MAC is a nice-to-have for a stable manual-add IP. Adopt later via Settings → Devices & Services → Add → ESPHome → 10.0.0.11:6053, no key (plaintext first; Noise PSK later — unencrypted ESPHome devices are NOT hard-disabled). No firewall/VLAN blocks: fedora + device share 10.0.0.0/24 flat L2; fedora's host firewall doesn't filter LAN ingress to :8123, and the native-API connection is HA→device outbound.

title: ESP-IDF OTA slot mechanism (EspOta: write, flip, rollback)
description: The OTA mechanism on ESP-IDF: use esp-idf-svc EspOta to write an image into the inactive OTA slot, mark it, reboot into it, and roll back on a failed boot. ESP-IDF supplies the partition, otadata, and bootloader machinery natively (why this supersedes the whole no_std OTA stack the old qqh epic pinned). SCOPE: only the local slot mechanism (image source may be an embedded blob or flash read here); the network fetch and update policy are a separate bead. Acceptance: an image is written to the inactive slot, booted, and a deliberately bad image rolls back, on the board. Depends on the std build and the workspace.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] partition table sized from the MEASURED release image (qhw.28 records it): two app slots + otadata fit 4 MB with a stated margin
- [ ] EspOta writes an image to the inactive slot, marks it, reboots into it (new version visible in the boot log)
- [ ] a checksum-corrupt image rolls back via the bootloader
- [ ] an image that BOOTS but fails its self-test triggers app-initiated rollback (mark-invalid path)
- [ ] power loss mid-slot-write leaves the device booting the prior good slot with intact otadata
- [ ] no network in this bead (fetch is qhw.23)

title: esphome-api: blocking frame codec over std::io
description: Implement the ESPHome native-API frame codec as a blocking reader/writer over std::io Read and Write, replacing the vendored tokio-util codec. Plaintext frame = 1-byte preamble 0x00, then varint payload-size, then varint message-type-id, then exactly payload-size bytes of protobuf — ONE length field, size BEFORE type (verified against developers.esphome.io protocol details and aioesphomeapi). Encrypted frames (preamble 0x01, 2-byte big-endian length) are handled by the Noise bead. Keep the byte-level encode/decode pure over buffers; the std::io pump is a thin wrapper, so the effect-audit domain boundary stays meaningful. Tests: golden known-answer frames captured from aioesphomeapi (round-trip alone only proves self-consistency), round-trip properties, malformed and short-read handling. Depends on the vendored crate and proto types.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] plaintext framing matches the REAL wire: 0x00, varint payload-size, varint message-type, payload — size before type, ONE length field (per developers.esphome.io + aioesphomeapi)
- [ ] known-answer test: encoding a fixed message is byte-exact against a CAPTURED aioesphomeapi plaintext frame, and decoding that captured frame yields the message (round-trip alone only proves self-consistency)
- [ ] round-trip property test across sizes: empty, 1-byte, many-byte payloads and varint length boundaries
- [ ] malformed preamble, truncated frame, oversized length -> typed errors, never a panic
- [ ] preamble 0x01 (encrypted) recognized and cleanly rejected until the Noise bead (qhw.10)
- [ ] byte-level encode/decode is pure over buffers; the std::io pump is a thin wrapper (keeps the effect-audit domain boundary meaningful)
close_reason: Plaintext frame codec landed: pure frame.rs encode/decode + thin frame_io.rs std::io pump. Known-answer test against CAPTURED aioesphomeapi frames (byte-exact both ways), proptest round-trip across sizes/varint boundaries, typed errors for bad preamble/oversized/truncated (never panics), preamble 0x01 rejected for the Noise bead. 34 tests + clippy clean. Commit 9c00805.

title: esphome-api: pure connection FSM + host value-tests

comments.text:

The accept loop needs only portable std (TcpListener, threads, timeouts), so it follows the plant-shell precedent (qhw.21): a host crate, verified on the host, cross-compiling to esp-idf std unchanged. The hex-lint gate agrees (std shell = driving-adapter, not infra). firmware-infra stays WiFi/mDNS/OTA (the esp-idf-svc services); the composition root (qhw.9) pulls esphome-server by path.

- [x] AC1 serves any Registry, zero project-specific logic — the `Device` port (device_info/list_messages/state_messages); no plant/led logic in src.
- [x] AC2 cap + reject (cap+1)th + reclaim on leave — serves_up_to_the_cap_and_rejects_beyond_it, reclaims_a_slot_when_a_connection_ends. AtomicUsize slot counter + drop-guard.
- [x] AC3 stalled client reaped, subsequent connection succeeds — reaps_a_stalled_client_and_keeps_serving (partial frame + stall -> reaped within the idle window; healthy client then served).

title: Soil calibration: capture dry/wet points + persist to NVS
description: Make the moisture percent MEANINGFUL. Soil probes vary per unit and drift (the resistive Earth pads also corrode), so dry_raw/wet_raw must be captured per probe, not hardcoded. Add a device-side calibration flow: capture a dry reading (probe in air/dry soil) and a wet reading (probe in water/wet soil), triggered by the ON-BOARD BUTTON (BtnA G37 / BtnB G39); an HA Button/Number-entity trigger is out of scope until the registry grows those entity types. Persist the Calibration to ESP-IDF NVS so it survives reboot; the sampler reads the persisted calibration. NVS writes must be power-loss-safe (a torn write must never produce a degenerate pair — pairs with plant-core's defined dry==wet behavior). The raw MVP may ship with hardcoded constants; this refines it into a usable monitor.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] dry + wet capture triggered by the ON-BOARD button writes Calibration to NVS (an HA Button/Number-entity trigger is deferred until those entity types exist in the registry)
- [ ] calibration survives a clean power cycle; the sampler uses the persisted values
- [ ] power-loss-safe: an interrupted NVS write leaves the previous calibration or safe defaults, never a corrupt/degenerate pair; boot with corrupted/zeroed NVS falls back to defaults without panic (pairs with plant-core's defined dry==wet behavior)
- [ ] partial capture handled: dry captured but wet not yet -> defined behavior, no bogus percent
- [ ] after capture: ~0% in the dry state, ~100% in the wet state; both probe orderings handled

title: plant-core: Moisture entity + calibration (pure)
description: Start the no_std, zero-dependency plant-core crate with the value types only: Moisture, a u8 newtype with invariant 0..=100, and Calibration (dry_raw, wet_raw), plus to_percent(raw, cal) using integer-only i32 math (no float, no libm), clamped and branch-safe for either calibration order (the Earth Unit is a RESISTIVE probe — expect wet to read higher — but wiring varies per unit, so the math must not assume a direction). Degenerate calibration (dry_raw == wet_raw, e.g. zeroed NVS) must return a defined value, never divide by zero. Tests: property tests proving the result is always in 0..=100, dry_raw maps to 0, wet_raw maps to 100, monotonicity, out-of-range clamps. The SoilSensor port and the sampler step are a separate bead. effect-audit must pass with role=domain. Pure host work; start immediately.

- [ ] to_percent is integer-only i32 math (no float, no libm), clamped
- [ ] proptests: result always 0..=100 for any (raw, cal); dry_raw->0; wet_raw->100; monotone between; clamps outside; BOTH calibration orders handled (resistive Earth probe expected wet-high, but the math must not assume a direction)
- [ ] degenerate calibration defined: dry_raw == wet_raw (e.g. zeroed NVS) returns a defined value, no panic/divide-by-zero; the proptest generator explicitly covers equal and adjacent endpoints
- [ ] plant-core added to root Cargo.toml members; just test runs it; cargo test green on host

title: Gate Earth-probe power: energize only during sampling
description: The Earth Unit is a RESISTIVE soil probe; m5 docs state the electrodes are not anti-corrosive, POC-grade, and should not sit in a humid environment for long. Constant DC bias across the exposed pads electrolyzes them — a 24/7 plant monitor corrodes the probe and drifts the calibration within weeks. Energize the probe only during a sampling window and keep it unpowered between samples. Candidate mechanisms (implementer's choice): gate the Grove 5V rail via the AXP192 boost/EXTEN path in board-support, a GPIO-driven high-side switch, or duty-cycled sampling with an empirically-determined settle delay before each read. The pure plant-core step stays untouched — gating is shell work in the sampler/adapter. Found by cross-model review (2026-07-03); sources: docs.m5stack.com/en/unit/earth, shop.m5stack.com Earth listing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] probe is unpowered between samples (verified at the Grove 5V pin or via AXP192 state)
- [ ] settle delay after power-on determined empirically; gated readings match always-on readings within a stated tolerance
- [ ] duty cycle documented (powered window vs sample period)
- [ ] gating lives in the shell; the pure plant-core step is untouched

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
SEAM SCAFFOLDED (qhw.5 follow-on) — this bead is now a clean fill-in.

The power-gating seam is in place and host-tested; qhw.31 only needs to supply a
real power mechanism and tune the settle. Nothing in the adapter or plant-core
moves.

What exists now:
- firmware-core::probe_power::ProbePower — the driven port: energize(&mut) /
  deenergize(&mut), associated Error. Doc contract: energize() returns only once
  the rail is UP AND SETTLED, so the caller reads immediately after.
- firmware-core::probe_power::gated_read(power, read) — energize -> read ->
  deenergize, and de-energize runs on EVERY exit path. If the read fails the
  probe is still powered down before the error propagates (corrosion-safety); a
  failed energize skips the read; a de-energize error surfaces only when the read
  succeeded (a stuck-on probe is its own hazard). Pure, 4 host tests.
- adapters::probe_power::AlwaysOn — ProbePower<Error=EspError> no-op default; the
  probe stays powered, but EarthUnit ALREADY routes every read through gated_read.
- adapters::adc::EarthUnit<'d, P: ProbePower<Error=EspError>> — read_raw() =
  gated_read(power, || oversampled_mean(64, || channel.read_raw())). One brief
  power pulse per logical reading.

What qhw.31 implements:
1. A real ProbePower<Error=EspError> whose energize() powers the Grove/probe rail
   AND blocks for the empirically-tuned settle before returning; deenergize()
   cuts it. Candidate homes: board-support (AXP192 EXTEN/boost rail, pairs with
   qhw.20) or adapters::probe_power (a GPIO high-side switch).
2. Swap AlwaysOn -> the real impl in the plant-monitor composition root. That is
   the ENTIRE wiring change — EarthUnit is generic over P and does not move.

Design decision (why per-read, not per-window): EarthUnit::read_raw() already
returns one denoised value (64 internal conversions), so gating the burst = one
brief power pulse per logical reading, and the sampler (qhw.21) stays oblivious.
If qhw.21 later takes K>1 temporal samples per interval, that is K brief pulses —
still preferable to one long powered window for corrosion.

Acceptance mapping:
- "unpowered between samples" -> gated_read de-energizes after every read; the
  probe is off across the sampler's interval. Verify at the Grove pin / AXP192.
- "settle delay empirical; gated == always-on within tolerance" -> settle lives
  inside energize(); tune it, then compare gated readings to the AlwaysOn
  baseline (dry ~1017, wet ~930 from qhw.5).
- "duty cycle documented" -> powered window (settle + ~64-sample burst, tens of
  ms) vs sample period (the sampler interval).
- "gating in the shell, plant-core untouched" -> ProbePower + gated_read are
  firmware-core/adapter; plant-core is unchanged. Already satisfied.

It cannot. hex-lint 'explain infra': an infra crate may depend ONLY on infra, and

- The AXP192 holds its rail state through ESP32 deep sleep. The duty-cycle refactor

  is idle. The bias comes from the probe's own 10k pull-up, not from read_raw --
  sampling less often achieves nothing.

title: Detect a disconnected/floating soil probe and surface it distinctly
description:
The moisture pipeline (qhw.21) cannot tell a *disconnected* Earth Unit from a real reading. Verified on-board 2026-07-04: with the probe unplugged, GPIO33 floats to a readable voltage, the ADC oneshot read *succeeds*, and the pipeline publishes a plausible-but-false value (100% under the provisional calibration). A pulled or failed probe therefore reports garbage silently instead of alerting.

Note the boundary this must respect: the sampler's staleness / `unavailable` path (qhw.21) fires only on a read *error* or a dead sampler thread — a floating-but-readable pin is neither. Disconnect detection has to happen at the ADC boundary, not in the shell.

Goal: the ADC adapter (or a sibling presence check) detects a floating/disconnected probe and surfaces it as *not a valid reading* — distinct from a genuine 0%/100%, and ideally distinct from generic staleness. The cleanest wiring reuses what qhw.21 already built: on a disconnected verdict the adapter returns a read error (or a `Disconnected` variant), the sampler skips the publish, the shared cache goes `unavailable`, and consumers (display, HA sensor) show unavailable rather than a false value. If HA should distinguish "disconnected" from "stale", add one explicit variant rather than collapsing both to a bare error.

Candidate mechanisms (context, not a prescription — pick what proves out on the bench):
- **Excitation delta via qhw.31 power-gating** — sample with probe power OFF then ON; a connected resistive probe's reading moves with excitation, a floating pin does not. Tests the actual sensing element and is near-free once qhw.31's switch exists. Likely the primary mechanism.
- **Internal pull-up/pull-down delta** on the RTC pad (GPIO33) — read once with pull-up, once with pull-down; a low-impedance connected source gives a small delta, a floating pin a large one. Pure chip feature, no extra hardware, but it biases a normal measurement (run it as a separate check), thresholds are empirical, and confirm esp-idf-hal 0.46 cleanly toggles the RTC pull around the oneshot AdcChannelDriver.
- **External bias/pull resistor** — deterministic fallback that turns "floating" into a fixed out-of-band value; trivial firmware, but a hardware change rather than a chip feature.
- (Footnote) GPIO33 is touch channel T8 — capacitive presence is possible but noisy and needs pin-mode juggling; likely overkill.

Acceptance:
- With the Earth Unit physically disconnected, consumers see the probe as unavailable/disconnected — NOT a plausible moisture percentage — proven on-board (unplug flips the served state within a bounded number of periods).
- A genuinely connected probe (dry, damp, wet) is never mis-flagged as disconnected — proven on-board across the range, with a clear margin between the connected band and the disconnected verdict.
- The connectivity logic that can be host-tested is host-tested (e.g. the pure delta/threshold decision as a function of the raw reads); the irreducibly on-target part stays a thin adapter shell.
- No domain logic leaks: the disconnect decision lives at the driven-adapter boundary; plant-core stays framework-free.
- Disconnect thresholds/margins are documented (bench-measured), not magic numbers.

Depends on qhw.31 (probe power-gating) for the excitation-delta path. Related: qhw.21 (sampler + staleness path this plugs into), qhw.29 (real calibration).

comments.author: elendal
comments.text:
PREMISE INCOMPLETE (2026-07-08) — this bead scopes the work to catching a FLOATING
pin. That is one of three fault modes, and the one that actually bit us is a
different one.

Read the schematic (now recorded in kb/sources/m5-earth-unit.md): the Earth Unit
regulates Grove 5 V to 3.3 V locally (HT7533) and pulls Ain up through R1 = 10k,
with the soil in the LOWER leg. Therefore:

  raw = 4095  electrodes OPEN (corroded through, or soil past the readable range).
              R1 pulls Ain to 3.3 V, above the ADC's 12 dB ceiling. Reads as 0%.
  raw = 0     probe rail DOWN (failed to energize). No pull-up, Ain at ground.
              Reads as 100%. This one only becomes reachable once qhw.31 lands.
  mid-scale   Grove cable UNPLUGGED. R1 leaves with the probe; GPIO33 floats.
              This is the case the bead's 'verified on-board 2026-07-04, publishes
              a plausible-but-false 100%' observation captured.

So 'unplugged' and 'dead probe' sit at OPPOSITE ends. A real 24/7 failure (2026-07-08:
electrodes electrolyzed open after ~2 days of AlwaysOn bias) pinned the ceiling and
the monitor served a serene 0% to HA for two days.

PARTIALLY LANDED. The two rails are now rejected at the adapter boundary, exactly
where this bead asks: firmware_core::saturation::unsaturated (pure, host-tested,
proptested) + adapters::adc::ReadError::Saturated, applied OUTSIDE gated_read so the
corrosion-safety contract stays intact. The shell needed zero changes -- sampler
already publishes nothing on a failed read, so the cache ages out and both the TFT
and the HA sensor go unavailable. Verified on-device: serial logs the rejection and
the native API flips missing_state=false -> true.
Finding: kb/findings/saturated-adc-reading-is-not-a-measurement.md.

STILL OPEN, and the harder half: a floating/unplugged probe lands mid-scale and
sails straight through a rails check. The excitation-delta mechanism this bead
already proposes is now FREE -- qhw.31's confirmed EXTEN gating gives us rail-off /
rail-on sampling. A connected probe's reading moves with excitation; a floating pin's
does not. That is the primary mechanism; keep the pure delta/threshold decision
host-testable.

Also note for the HA-facing AC: SensorStateResponse carries only state +
missing_state, so a sensor entity CANNOT express 'disconnected' distinctly from
'stale'. Collapsing both to unavailable is the protocol's only option today; an
explicit variant needs a second (binary_sensor) entity.

Scope consequence worth deciding: rejecting the ceiling means a genuinely DRY pot
now reads unavailable rather than 0%, because with R1=10k the node leaves the ADC's
usable range above ~30k of soil resistance -- and the provisional dry_raw=2600
(~15k) sits below that cliff. Truthful, but the watering alert must treat
unavailable as actionable. Real fix is qhw.29 calibration, possibly a smaller
pull-up.

title: Carry the raw ADC count alongside percent through the moisture pipeline
description:
The display (qhw.6) must show the raw ADC count as well as the moisture percent, but today the raw count is destroyed inside the pure sampling step: plant-core::sampler::step computes the raw mean, calibrates it to a Moisture (percent only), and drops the raw u16. Nothing downstream of step ever sees raw.

Introduce a Measurement value object that pairs the raw ADC mean with its calibrated Moisture, and thread it from step through the freshness Reading, the fresh policy, and the SharedMoisture cache, so every cache reader can see both raw and percent. This is domain provenance, not presentation: the raw count is exactly what qhw.29 (dry/wet calibration capture) and qhw.32 (floating-probe detection) operate on; percent stays derived.

Constraints:
- report-on-change stays keyed on percent, not raw jitter, so a steady plant still produces no native-API traffic.
- The native API keeps serving percent only (Option<f32>); raw does not reach Home Assistant.
- Host-tested: the whole change is proven off-device with cargo test (unit + property + Gherkin). Add coverage that Measurement round-trips raw and that fresh preserves it.

Acceptance:
- Measurement { raw, moisture } exists in plant-core with raw()/moisture()/percent() accessors and its invariants.
- step/Reading/fresh/SharedMoisture carry Measurement; SharedMoisture::latest yields Option<Measurement>.
- plant-monitor composition root still compiles and serves percent to HA unchanged.
- just test is green; a scenario asserts raw is carried alongside percent.
close_reason: Measurement threads raw+percent through step/Reading/fresh/SharedMoisture; host-tested (unit+property+Gherkin), raw flowing on-device.

title: Bounded ring-buffer infrastructure for observability streams
description:
Observability needs somewhere to put records that are produced faster than they are consumed, on a chip with 520 KB of SRAM and no PSRAM. Log streaming (the SubscribeLogs bead) is the first consumer; a short history of recent observations, for the display or a diagnostics entity, is a plausible second. Build the buffer once, properly, rather than open-coding a VecDeque behind a Mutex in each.

The shape of the problem:
- PRODUCERS are threads that must never block and must never allocate on the hot path: the `log` facade (called from the sampler thread, the display thread, the WiFi driver, an ISR-adjacent context), and the sampler itself. A producer that blocks on a slow TCP consumer would stall soil sampling; a producer that allocates can OOM a 520 KB chip under load.
- CONSUMERS are the native-API server's per-connection threads, which come and go as Home Assistant connects and disconnects, and which may fall arbitrarily far behind or vanish mid-drain.
- OVERFLOW IS NORMAL, not an error. A slow or absent consumer must cause the OLDEST records to be dropped, never the newest, and never backpressure onto the producer. The number dropped must be observable — a silently truncated log is a false green, and this project has already been bitten once by a signal that looked healthy while lying.

Requirements:
- Bounded, fixed capacity, chosen at construction. No unbounded growth under any consumer behaviour.
- Overwrite-oldest on overflow, with a monotonically increasing dropped/lost counter a consumer can read to learn it missed N records.
- A consumer that disconnects must not leak, wedge the ring, or stall producers.
- NO unsafe. If lock-freedom cannot be had safely, a short critical section is acceptable — correctness over cleverness — but the producer's critical section must be O(1) and must not span an I/O call.
- The data structure itself is PURE: it names no HAL, no socket, no log crate. Host-tested, including the overflow and slow-consumer paths, with property tests for the invariants (capacity never exceeded; FIFO order among surviving records; dropped-count exactly accounts for the difference between pushed and observed).
- Both the firmware workspace and the host workspace need it (the server host that drains it is a portable host crate), so pick a home that satisfies hex-lint's role matrix for both. Note infra may depend only on infra; a pure zero-dep structure has options.

Zero/one/many: prove the empty ring, the single record, the exactly-full ring, and the wrapped-many-times ring. Two consumers count as many.

Open question for the implementer: whether a single shared ring with per-consumer read cursors beats a broadcast fan-out of independent rings. The former bounds memory by capacity; the latter isolates a slow consumer from a fast one. State the choice and why.

title: Fault-aware Observation model: separate 'probe is lying' from 'sampler is dead'
description:
SharedMoisture::latest() -> Option<Measurement> is an information-destroying boundary. It collapses four distinct states into None, and every consumer (the TFT, the Home Assistant sensor, the serial heartbeat) then independently re-derives a worse answer from that None:

  - nothing sampled since boot
  - the last reading aged out (the sampler thread is dead or hung)
  - the sampler is alive and the probe returned a fault (saturated at a rail, or the ADC errored)
  - a genuine measurement

REGRESSION THIS FIXES. Before the saturation guard landed, missing_state=false over the native API proved the sampler thread was alive: a fresh cache implies a running writer. That inference was used, on 2026-07-08, to prove the firmware was healthy while the probe was dead. The guard broke it: sample_once publishes only on a SUCCESSFUL read, so a rejected saturated reading now publishes nothing and the cache ages out — indistinguishable over the wire from a panicked sampler thread. We traded a false green for an ambiguous red. Freshness (is the writer alive?) and health (is the probe honest?) are orthogonal axes and Option can only carry one.

Goal: make the observation a first-class domain value that carries both axes, publish it on EVERY sampler cycle (fault included, stamped), and let each adapter render it. Then a fresh fault means 'sampler alive, probe lying' and staleness recovers its precise meaning: 'the writer stopped'.

Shape (illustrative, not prescriptive):
  Observation = Fresh(Measurement) | Faulted(ProbeFault) | Stale | NeverSampled
  ProbeFault  = OverRange | UnderRange | Unreadable

NAMING MATTERS HERE. Call it OverRange, not OpenCircuit. raw=4095 means 'above the readable range', which is EITHER corroded electrodes OR bone-dry soil — kb/findings/saturated-adc-reading-is-not-a-measurement.md establishes exactly that, and the type must not claim more than the evidence supports. Likewise UnderRange (raw=0) is 'below the readable range', which after probe power-gating lands will also be the signature of a rail that failed to energize.

Design question the implementer must answer: how does the fault cross the SoilSensor port without dragging EspError into a framework-free domain? The port has an associated Error type today, and plant-shell already bounds it on Display for logging. Classification belongs at the boundary, where the adapter alone knows what its own error means — adapters::adc::ReadError maps Saturated(Ceiling)->OverRange, Saturated(Floor)->UnderRange, Adc(_)->Unreadable. Keep the adapter's rich error for the log line; give the domain the classified fault.

Blast radius, all of which is in scope:
- plant-core: the Observation + ProbeFault types; the freshness rule becomes a four-way decision rather than an Option; Reading carries an outcome, not just a Measurement.
- plant-shell: the sampler publishes on every cycle; SharedMoisture serves an Observation.
- plant-core ports: MoistureDisplay::show takes an Observation, so the glass can name the fault instead of showing a bare 'unavailable'.
- adapters: st7789 renders the fault reason; adc classifies its ReadError.
- composition root: the heartbeat logs the observation; the native-API SensorSource maps Fresh -> Some(percent) and everything else -> None (unchanged HA behaviour for now; the fault ENTITY is a separate bead).

Acceptance:
- Over the native API, a faulted probe and a dead sampler thread are distinguishable without attaching a serial cable. Proven on-device with the corroded probe (Faulted) and with the sampler deliberately stopped (Stale).
- The TFT names the fault rather than showing a bare unavailable placeholder.
- gated_read's corrosion-safety contract is untouched; the probe is still de-energized on every exit path.
- Pure rules stay pure and host-tested: the four-way freshness decision is a total function of (last, now, max_age), property-tested. Zero/one/many on the sampler's publish path.
- No regression in the existing Gherkin feature (plant-core/tests/features/moisture.feature).
close_reason: done

LANDED 2026-07-09 — with ONE acceptance criterion corrected, not quietly dropped.

What shipped:

  W plant_monitor: sampler alive, probe faulted — serving unavailable: reading above

where it previously read the ambiguous 'moisture unavailable'.

faulted probe and a dead sampler thread are distinguishable without attaching a

reaches the adapter, but nobody has looked at the glass. Someone should confirm it
reads FAULT / RAW HIGH.

title: Diagnostic entities: surface raw count, probe fault, RSSI and uptime to Home Assistant
description:
The device serves exactly one entity — a soil moisture percentage. Everything an operator needs to decide whether to TRUST that percentage is discarded at the API boundary. The raw ADC count is carried all the way through Measurement (qhw.33) and then thrown away; the fault reason exists for microseconds inside sample_once and goes to a serial port nobody is attached to; there is no way to ask the device how long it has been up, or how good its WiFi link is.

Concretely: on 2026-07-08 a corroded probe served a serene 0% for two days. Home Assistant had nothing to alert on, because a flat 0% is a valid moisture reading. A binary_sensor with device_class 'problem' would have fired on day one.

Goal: expose the diagnostics HA already knows how to render, graph, and alert on — so the operator never has to reflash the board to find out what it thinks is wrong.

Entities to add (all but the first tagged entity_category=diagnostic so HA files them away):
- sensor.soil_raw — the raw ADC count behind the percent. Already in Measurement. Its provenance value is exactly why qhw.33 kept it.
- binary_sensor.probe_fault — device_class 'problem'. True whenever the observation is Faulted. This is the one that turns a silent lie into an alert.
- text_sensor.probe_status — the fault reason ('above readable range', 'sampler stale', ...). Gives a human the WHY without a serial cable.
- sensor.wifi_rssi (dBm) and sensor.uptime (s). Uptime alone answers 'did it reboot?', which could not be answered at all during the 2026-07-08 investigation.

Context the implementer needs:
- esphome_api::Device is ALREADY multi-entity: device_info() + list_messages() -> Vec<ListMessage> + state_messages() -> Vec<StateMessage>. SensorDevice is a single-sensor convenience impl, not a limit. The composition root needs a real multi-entity Device impl; SensorDevice may survive as a convenience or be retired.
- ListMessage/StateMessage carry a BinarySensor variant, but it is explicitly marked 'UNVERIFIED placeholder — no entity produces this yet'. It must be exercised against the real client before it is trusted. There is NO TextSensor variant at all — the proto types exist (ListEntitiesTextSensorResponse=18, TextSensorStateResponse=27) but the enums do not carry them.
- The aioesphomeapi oracle (esphome-api/tests/aioesphomeapi_oracle.rs) is how a new entity type earns the right to drop 'UNVERIFIED'. A new entity type that has not been round-tripped against the real Home Assistant client is not done. Extend the oracle to assert each new entity is listed AND that its state arrives.
- entity_category lives on the ListEntities*Response messages; check the vendored proto rather than guessing the field.

Acceptance:
- HA adopts the device and shows every entity; the oracle proves each new entity type lists and reports state against the real client, so no variant stays UNVERIFIED.
- Pulling the probe, or leaving it corroded, raises binary_sensor.probe_fault and populates text_sensor.probe_status — verified on-device.
- The moisture sensor's existing behaviour (missing_state when not Fresh) is unchanged.
- Entity keys stay stable across reboots (object_id hash), so HA does not orphan entities. The existing golden_ids/entity_keys tests must cover the new object_ids.

title: Stream device logs over the native API (SubscribeLogsRequest/Response)
description:
Real ESPHome devices stream their logs over the native API; ours cannot. SubscribeLogsRequest (msg 28) and SubscribeLogsResponse (msg 29) are in the generated id table and in the proto, but esphome_api::Inbound::decode drops them into Inbound::Other, where handle() silently ignores them.

The cost is not theoretical. Diagnosing the corroded probe on 2026-07-08 required: a USB cable, espflash driving DTR/RTS (a plain `cat /dev/ttyUSB0` reads nothing), and a board reset that destroyed the very failure state under investigation. The one number that mattered — raw=4095 — was visible ONLY on a serial line. With log streaming, the whole investigation is one subscription against a board left untouched on a windowsill.

Goal: a connected client (Home Assistant, the `aioesphomeapi` client, or an agent) can subscribe to the device's log stream over TCP and receive the same records the serial console shows, at a requested level.

Context the implementer needs:
- The pure side is small: an Inbound::SubscribeLogs variant, an Outbound::LogEntry, and the FSM rule that a subscribed connection receives log records. All host-testable in esphome-api with no socket.
- The effectful side is the interesting part. The `log` crate's facade is global and is called from arbitrary threads (sampler, display, WiFi driver). Records must reach zero or more per-connection threads WITHOUT blocking the caller and WITHOUT allocating on the hot path — a logging call that waits on a slow TCP consumer would stall soil sampling. This is what the ring-buffer bead (qhw.34) exists to supply; consume it, do not open-code a Mutex<VecDeque>.
- On-device, EspLogger is already installed by the composition root. Whatever ships must TEE: records keep going to the serial console AND reach the ring. Losing the serial console to gain the network one is not a trade worth making.
- Records dropped because a consumer fell behind must be reported to that consumer (see qhw.34's dropped-count). A log stream with a silent hole is a lie of exactly the kind this project has already been burned by.
- SubscribeLogsResponse carries a level and the message bytes; check the vendored proto for the exact fields and whether HA expects the ANSI-coloured or the plain form.
- Level filtering is per-subscription (the request carries the level the client wants), so the fan-out must filter per consumer, not globally.

Acceptance:
- The real `aioesphomeapi` client, via the existing oracle harness, subscribes and receives log records emitted by the device, at the level it asked for and no more verbose.
- The serial console still shows everything it showed before.
- A subscriber that stops draining does not block the sampler thread, does not grow memory without bound, and learns how many records it missed.
- The board can be diagnosed over WiFi alone: with the probe faulted, a subscriber sees the sampler's rejection line without a USB cable ever being attached. Proven on-device.
- No unsafe; the pure protocol half is host-tested apart from the transport, as the rest of esphome-api is.

Open items: confirm UbiHome ships committed prost .rs (no build-time protoc), enable exactly one api-version feature, confirm noise-rust license is MIT-compatible. Pure host work.

- [ ] api.proto provenance pinned: aioesphomeapi commit recorded, MIT license text retained (NEVER esphome/esphome, GPLv3)

description: Shell adapter implementing the plant-core SoilSensor port over the ESP-IDF oneshot ADC. Read the Earth Unit analog output on GPIO33, which is ADC1 channel 5. - [ ] reads ADC1 ch5 / GPIO33 at 12 dB attenuation; oversampled mean of N samples (N documented)

comments.text:
Implemented `adapters::adc::EarthUnit` (firmware/adapters/src/adc.rs) implementing
`plant_core::SoilSensor` over the ESP-IDF oneshot ADC. type Error = EspError.
ADC1 ch5 / GPIO33 @ 12 dB (DB_12), Calibration::None, mean of N=64 rapid reads.

ADC1 is enforced by the TYPE: the channel is `ADCCH5<ADCU1>`, so constructing the
adapter over `peripherals.adc2` does not compile. The "must be ADC1 / ADC2 dies
under WiFi" requirement is therefore structural, not a runtime hope.

Oversampling (N=64) extracted as a pure, hardware-free reduction
(firmware/adapters/src/oversample.rs) and host-unit-tested (4/4: one, many, mean
floors, error short-circuit) — the esp-idf-* deps + the `adc` module are gated to
`cfg(target_os = "espidf")` so `cargo test` off-target runs the reduction without
the on-target HAL. This oversampling is orthogonal to plant-core's temporal
averaging in sampler::step: this suppresses per-conversion electrical noise, that
smooths readings taken seconds apart.

Open item RESOLVED: esp-idf-hal 0.46 DOES expose ESP32 line-fitting calibration
(config::Calibration::Line, backed by eFuse Vref — board-info reports "VRef
calibration in efuse" on this chip, rev v1.1). Curve-fitting is NOT offered on the
plain ESP32 (C3/C6/S3 only). We deliberately take RAW COUNTS (Calibration::None):
the port contract is raw, the domain pins the dry/wet endpoints itself. Line-cal
only maps raw->mV, which the raw-count contract neither needs nor wants.

ON-BOARD VERIFICATION (flashed to /dev/ttyUSB0, esp32 rev v1.1):
  air (dangling): raw = 4095, spread 0
  dry soil:       raw ~1017  (band [1015, 1021], spread 6 counts)
  wet soil:       raw ~930   (band [927, 938])
Monotonically ordered and disjoint: 4095 > 1017 > 930. Direction RECORDED =
dry-high / wet-low (the bead guessed wet-high; moisture.rs is direction-agnostic,
so the observed direction is authoritative). Dry<->wet minimum gap ~77 counts, no
band overlap. Per-read spread at constant moisture <= ~0.25% FS — the 64x
oversampling suppressing the ESP32 ADC's native +-30..60-count jitter.

Verified locally: xtensa release build + clippy clean; host oversample tests 4/4.

up, so the reading was taken WiFi-down. That clause exists only to catch an
accidental ADC2 wiring (ADC2 errors while WiFi is active); here ADC2 is
unrepresentable in the type, so the check is structurally moot and will be
exercised for free once qhw.7 brings WiFi up and qhw.9/qhw.21 keep the ADC1 read
path running online. Closing on: monotonic behavior confirmed on-board + ADC1
guaranteed by type. Honest status: live WiFi-coexistence not re-observed.

comments.text:
ON-DEVICE ADOPTION VERIFIED (the qhw.9 on-device AC). Chased an HA "Unable to connect... include an api section" error to root:

1. Board ran stale fw (commit b4afd17, the qhw.7 build): mDNS advertised _esphomelib._tcp:6053 but no server behind it -> TCP reset. Reflashed HEAD.
2. After reflash the server bound 0.0.0.0:6053 but dropped every handshake with EOF, no panic/reboot in serial -> pump was returning before the first reply.

FIX (esphome-server/src/server.rs): dropped the dup - both halves borrow one &TcpStream (pump is single-threaded: reads then writes, never concurrently; std impls Read/Write for &TcpStream). Portable, no IDF flag, no unsafe. write_all/broadcast_changes made generic over W: io::Write.

description: Future third project: a controllable moving rover that exposes telemetry and non-realtime controls to Home Assistant through the same esphome-api registry (Switch, Number, Cover, sensor telemetry). The shared foundation (std esp-idf, hexagonal domain behind ports, native-API telemetry) does not preclude this. IMPORTANT divergence: the M5StickC Plus is NOT a flight controller (ESP32-PICO-D4 with a single MPU6886 IMU, no magnetometer or barometer, and HA is the wrong control path for flight). Keep any real-time control loop local to the firmware, keep telemetry/config on the native-API path, and expect different hardware for the eventual ArduPilot-style flight phase. Not designed yet; a placeholder to hold the roadmap so the foundation is not wired to require HA in the control path.

title: Scope rover hardware plus local control path (spike)
description: Decide the rover hardware (motor driver, chassis, and for the later flight phase an IMU with magnetometer and barometer) and the local real-time control loop that stays off the Home Assistant path; define which telemetry and controls surface as native-API entities. Spike only; blocks nothing now.

title: Verify the remaining five orientation faces on the board
description:
The orientation readout names a resting face from which accelerometer axis carries gravity.
The mapping from axes to face names lives in one place (orientation_core::facing_of, with the
convention documented on the Facing type).

Only ONE pose has been verified on the metal so far: the board flat on its back reads
z = +1050 mg and reports SCREEN UP, so +Z = out of the screen is confirmed.

The other five faces rest on an ASSUMED convention:
  +X = toward the top of the stick (away from USB-C)  -> Inverted / Upright
  +Y = out of the stick's left edge                   -> LeftEdge / RightEdge

Verify each by turning the board and comparing the label against the signed X/Y/Z bars the
screen already shows (they are on the glass precisely so this is checkable by eye). The
serial heartbeat logs the same vector every 2 s if a record is wanted.

If a face is wrong, the fix is confined to facing_of plus its unit tests and the feature
file - no adapter or driver change. Also worth noting: z reads ~1050 mg at rest rather than
1000, a ~5% uncalibrated scale/offset typical of this part. It is well inside
REST_TOLERANCE_MG so it misclassifies nothing, but a zero-g/one-g calibration would be the
follow-on if the numbers themselves need to be trusted.
close_reason: done

title: Surface a lost IMU signal on the orientation glass, not just in the log
description:
The orientation sampler logs a failed IMU read and skips the cycle, leaving the last good
pose on the glass. That is the right call for the transient single I2C glitch it almost
always is, and it matches the fail-visible policy spawn_display and spawn_power_watch already
follow.

The cost is that a PERSISTENTLY dead sensor leaves a frozen but entirely plausible readout:
the bars sit still, the face label reads confidently, and nothing on the screen says the
numbers stopped being true. It is findable only in the serial log.

Wanted: a staleness clock in the shell (time since the last successful publish) and a
"NO SIGNAL" state on OrientationView that the screen draws distinctly - the same way Facing
already distinguishes "I cannot say" (Tilted/Moving) from a named pose. The display already
colours an unsettled face amber, so the vocabulary exists.

This is the one honesty gap knowingly left in the readout.
close_reason: done

title: Repoint five stale kb finding check: paths after the platform carve-out
description:
Five kb/findings carry `check:` commands that reference paths from before the platform
carve-out, so `just kb checks` reports 5 pre-existing failures on a clean tree:

  mipidsi-rectangle-fill-costs-an-address-window  -> plant-display/src/..., plant-shell/src/display.rs
  saturated-adc-reading-is-not-a-measurement      -> firmware-core/src/..., firmware/adapters/src/adc.rs
  st7789-wants-rgb-colour-order                   -> firmware/adapters/src/st7789.rs
  ws2812-grb-byte-order                           -> domain/src/color.rs
  axp192-exten-gates-grove-5v                     -> firmware/board-support/src/axp192.rs

The claims are all still true; only the paths moved (platform/ and firmware/platform/ now).
Each is a one-line `check:` repoint.

This matters more than tidiness: a permanently red gate trains everyone to ignore it, and
the next finding that breaks for a REAL reason will look exactly like the noise. The checks
exist to make a finding falsifiable - five that cannot run are five findings nothing is
verifying.
close_reason: done

title: Choose a screen rotation from the settled pose
description:
The orientation readout is legible in one attitude only. Turn the stick and the picture stays
put, so a readout whose whole purpose is to be read while the board is being moved becomes
unreadable in four of the six poses it names.

Wanted: the pure half of the fix — which way is up on the glass, decided from gravity.

A ScreenRotation of the four quadrants, and a total function from the board's acceleration
plus the rotation currently showing to the rotation that should be. Nothing here touches a
panel or a layout; it is the same shape as facing_of, and belongs beside it.

Two rules the choice has to honour, both already in the crate's vocabulary:

- Only a SETTLED pose rotates the screen. Turning the board mid-air must not spin the picture
  — reuse the rest tolerance Facing already uses to tell Moving from a named face. A board in
  motion keeps whatever rotation it had.
- A board lying flat has no in-plane gravity to read a quadrant from (ScreenUp / ScreenDown
  put all of it on Z), so it must keep the rotation it had rather than snapping to a default.
  This is why the function takes the current rotation as an argument at all.

The mapping from a board axis to "up on the glass" is NOT derivable from first principles —
the panel is a 135x240 portrait part mounted rotated, so which edge the native landscape image
calls "up" is a fact about the hardware. Establish it on the metal the same way the six faces
were established (see the commit for stick-c-plus-verify-orientation-faces-cs0), and write the
evidence into the docs.
close_reason: done

title: A portrait layout for the orientation readout
description:
The rotation feature's largest piece: the orientation screen cannot be drawn in portrait today.

The panel is 240x135 with FONT_10X20, so a landscape line holds 24 characters. Rotated a
quarter turn it is 135 wide — THIRTEEN characters. The current layout puts a 10-character face
label and a 10-character angles field side by side on one header line, and each axis row is a
name, a 130px bar and a 6-character value across the full width. None of that fits in 13
columns, and layout.rs asserts as much at compile time:

    assert!(SCREEN_SIZE.width > SCREEN_SIZE.height, "the canvas is landscape once rotated");

Wanted: a second layout for the portrait quadrants, and a screen that draws through whichever
layout is current. The obvious shape is for the geometry to become a value the renderer is
handed rather than a module of constants it reads — but the compile-time invariant block is
the point of the current design and must survive in some form. A portrait layout that let a
bar collide with its value, or ran a field off an edge, has to fail the BUILD exactly as the
landscape one does today.

Sketch of what has to give in portrait: the header stacks onto two lines instead of one, the
bars shorten to roughly 65px, and the milli-g values keep their 6-character field because
truncating a reading into a plausible smaller number is the one thing they must never do.

The screenshot gallery (just screens) is the review surface — every quadrant should land in it,
so a layout that looks wrong is caught by looking rather than by holding the board.

Depends on the ScreenRotation type from the core bead.

Handoff prompt with the surrounding context, the constraints that were paid for, and the
gotchas: docs/plans/orientation-portrait-layout.md
close_reason: done

title: Rotate the panel in hardware when the pose settles
description:
The wiring that makes the rotation real: turn the panel when the settled pose says to.

Rotate in HARDWARE, via MADCTL (mipidsi set_orientation), not with a software transform. A
rotating DrawTarget wrapper maps rows onto columns, which destroys the fill_contiguous fast
path that kb/findings/mipidsi-rectangle-fill-costs-an-address-window.md exists to protect: the
readout paints ~13 700 pixels a frame and the render loop already warns when a paint overruns
its tick budget. A MADCTL rotation costs nothing per pixel.

The known hazard is the CGRAM offset. This panel's visible window sits at col 52 / row 40 in
the native portrait orientation, and panel.rs carries a long comment about a fight between what
the datasheet says the MADCTL bits mean and what the glass actually did. Those offsets are NOT
the same in portrait and landscape, so a runtime orientation change is walking straight back
into that. Expect to verify this on the board, not in a framebuffer — a wrong offset shows up
as a picture shifted by a few dozen pixels, or a stripe of stale CGRAM down one edge.

Also to settle here: the render loop repaints on a changed view, so the rotation has to reach
it as part of the view (or the loop has to learn about it), otherwise the first frame after a
rotation is a correctly-rotated panel still holding the previous quadrant's pixels.

Verify by flashing and turning the board through all four reading positions, plus a check that
nothing regressed: one boot marker, no watchdog, and no "paint took ... over the ... tick
budget" warnings while rotating.

Depends on the core and display beads.
close_reason: Superseded by the screen-rotation epic (stick-c-plus-screen-rotation-platform-ce1). This bead scoped hardware rotation to the orientation app alone; the decision since is that rotation is a platform capability all four apps get, so the panel work is ce1.4 and the orientation app turning end to end is ce1.5. Nothing here is lost — both hazards it named (the orientation-dependent CGRAM offsets, and the rotation having to reach the render loop as part of the compared unit so the first frame after a turn is not stale) are carried into those two beads and into docs/plans/screen-rotation-platform-capability.md.

title: The picture always faces the reader: screen rotation as a platform capability
description:
When the board's orientation changes, whatever the current app is showing should turn to
face the reader, in a layout built for the shape it is turning into. All four apps —
orientation, pomodoro, plant-monitor, host-monitor.

Today none of this reaches the glass. ScreenRotation, RotationSettler and the measured
UpAxis table are complete and host-tested in orientation-core but are wired into no
firmware; the device always renders Deg0. orientation-display has a portrait layout; the
other three display crates assert landscape at build time. Panel::new bakes
Rotation::Deg90 in as a compile-time literal and there is no runtime set_orientation
anywhere. The IMU is wired into one binary of four.

The capability belongs to the platform rather than to each app's view: rotation reaches
the render loop and is handed to whichever render function is installed, so no app author
can forget to honour it. That is the whole architectural decision this epic rests on.

Plan, with the verified inventory, the seam, the hazards and the open questions:
docs/plans/screen-rotation-platform-capability.md

title: Carve the rotation domain into platform-core
description:
ScreenRotation, RotationSettler and the measured UpAxis table live in
apps/orientation/orientation-core/src/rotation.rs, which is context = "orientation". Three
more apps are about to need them, and hex-lint makes a cross-context dependency illegal —
correctly, because which way up the board is being held is a fact about the BOARD, not
about one app's domain.

Move them to platform-core (role = domain, context = shared), where the Imu port and
Acceleration already live. No behaviour change: the measured UpAxis -> ScreenRotation table
is hardware truth that was paid for with a board in hand, and rotation.rs carries the
measurement and the reasoning. Carry both across intact.

Only three crates depend on orientation-core (orientation-display, orientation-shell, and
the orientation composition root), plus orientation-core's own cucumber suite. Nothing else
in either workspace does, so the blast radius is known and small.

Gate: just ci. hex-lint will confirm the roles still hold.
close_reason: done

title: A shared rotation source: publish the settled rotation from the IMU
description:
Something has to own the IMU, fold each reading into a RotationSettler and publish the
rotation the glass should be drawn at. Today that logic runs nowhere on the device: the
settler is exercised only by unit tests and the host screenshots example.

The existing orientation sampler (apps/orientation/orientation-shell/src/sampler.rs) is the
right shape but the wrong context — it is context = "orientation", so the other three apps
cannot use it. Generalize rather than copy: the Imu port and Acceleration already live in
platform-core/shared, so a shared driving-adapter can consume them without any dependency
on an app.

Wanted: any binary can spawn this and read back the current ScreenRotation, with the
settling behaviour (ROTATION_SETTLE_MS) intact so the picture does not spin mid-turn.

Note the 10 ms floor: CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=100 means a shorter thread period busy-waits
instead of yielding. Host tests cannot see it.

title: Rotation reaches the render loop, for every app
description:
The bead that makes the capability exist. No visual change lands with it.

Today Screen::show(state, elapsed) has no rotation parameter, so rotation can only reach a
renderer by riding inside the app's own state — which is what OrientationView.rotation does
now. That does not generalize: four apps would each re-implement it and nothing would catch
the one that forgot. A capability the platform supplies must not be forgettable by an app
author.

Wanted: rotation is an input to the render loop and is handed to whichever render function
is installed. It must participate in the loop's repaint suppression — a turn that does not
repaint leaves the previous quadrant's pixels on a correctly-rotated panel, which is the
failure mode this design exists to make unrepresentable.

All four apps' render functions take the rotation and select a layout with it; three of them
have only a landscape layout for now and select it unconditionally. OrientationView.rotation
is removed in the same change — it becomes the loop's business.

Touches platform-core (the Screen trait), platform-runtime (the loop and its Shown unit),
both Screen impls including the test fake, and all four display crates.

title: Turn the panel in hardware, with the offsets that go with each rotation
description:
Panel::new bakes Rotation::Deg90 in as a compile-time literal and applies a single CGRAM
offset pair, OFFSET_X = 52 / OFFSET_Y = 40, valid under that one rotation. There is no
set_orientation call anywhere in the crate. Wanted: a runtime path that turns the panel and
applies the offsets belonging to the new orientation.

Hardware MADCTL, not a rotating DrawTarget: a software transform maps rows onto columns and
destroys the fill_contiguous fast path at ~13 700 px/frame. See
kb/findings/mipidsi-rectangle-fill-costs-an-address-window.md.

REQUIRES ON-METAL VERIFICATION, and no host test can substitute. The framebuffer is below
the panel, so a wrong offset — a picture shifted by dozens of pixels, or a stripe of stale
CGRAM down one edge — is invisible to every test in the suite.

Precedent worth reading first: the colour-order bug
(kb/experiments/2026-07-09-panel-colour-order/). The factory driver and mipidsi set the same
MADCTL bit and the glass still rendered red as blue, because the pixel pipelines around the
bit differ. Rotation bits live in that same register. Derive nothing from the factory
driver; measure. Panel::colour_check is the model for a falsifiable on-glass test, and this
bead deserves its equivalent.

Also watch the 25 Hz tick budget: the loop already warns "paint took ... over the ... tick
budget" and that warning is the gate.

title: The orientation readout turns, end to end
description:
The first app that actually rotates on the glass, and the proof that the four beads under it
compose. The orientation app goes first because it is the one that already has both halves —
the IMU on its bus and a finished portrait layout — so it isolates the new wiring.

Wanted: pick the board up, stand it on its USB-C port, and the readout is drawn upright in
the portrait layout, having settled rather than spun on the way.

The user-visible acceptance is exactly that sentence. Verify it by holding the board, not by
reading a test report; then watch serial for a reboot loop and for the paint-budget warning
while turning it repeatedly.

Everything this needs exists once ce1.1-ce1.4 land. If this bead turns out to need new
domain logic, something above it was under-built.

title: A portrait layout for the pomodoro timer
description:
pomodoro-display asserts landscape at build time (layout.rs:35) and pins every origin
against the single global SCREEN_SIZE const. It needs a second layout for the narrow canvas,
the way orientation-display now has one.

The constraint that shapes it: the panel is 240x135 with FONT_10X20, so a landscape line
holds 24 characters and a portrait one holds THIRTEEN. Whatever the header does side by side
today, it cannot do in thirteen columns.

Follow the pattern orientation-display established (apps/orientation/orientation-display/src/layout.rs):
geometry becomes a Layout value the renderer is handed rather than a module of constants it
reads, with LANDSCAPE/PORTRAIT consts and the invariant block moved into a const fn every
layout is held to. The compile-time guarantee is the point and must survive: a portrait field
running off an edge, or a bar colliding with its value, has to fail the BUILD rather than the
eye.

The creature is the interesting part here — the pomodoro's right-hand region holds a sprite
that IS the status, and a 20x20 creature at a fixed origin is a different proposition on a
135px-wide canvas. Decide deliberately whether it keeps its size, moves, or goes.

just screens is the review surface: every state should land in the gallery in both shapes,
so a layout that looks wrong is caught by looking.

title: A portrait layout for the plant monitor
description:
plant-display asserts landscape at build time (layout.rs:44) and pins every origin against
the single global SCREEN_SIZE const. It needs a second layout for the narrow canvas.

Thirteen characters a line in portrait against twenty-four in landscape, at FONT_10X20.

Follow the pattern orientation-display established: geometry becomes a Layout value with
LANDSCAPE/PORTRAIT consts and an invariant block in a const fn every layout is held to, so a
field off an edge fails the BUILD. See apps/orientation/orientation-display/src/layout.rs.

Specific to this screen: the moisture reading and its four Observation states carry a
sparkline and a creature. A sparkline is width-hungry and degrades differently from text
when it loses half its columns — decide what it becomes rather than letting it be truncated.

Same rule as everywhere on this board: a value may never be truncated into a plausible-
looking smaller number. Abbreviate a label first.

just screens is the review surface; every Observation state should land in the gallery in
both shapes.

title: A portrait layout for the host monitor
description:
host-display asserts landscape at build time (layout.rs:99) and pins every origin against the
single global SCREEN_SIZE const. It needs a second layout for the narrow canvas.

This is the hardest of the three. The screen is one ROW PER HOST across the full width — a
layout whose whole premise is horizontal room — and portrait takes away nearly half of it
while giving back vertical space for more rows. Whether that is a better or worse readout at
thirteen columns is a design question, not a fitting exercise. It may be that this screen
shows FEWER hosts in more detail when turned, or that it does not rotate at all.

Follow the pattern orientation-display established: a Layout value, LANDSCAPE/PORTRAIT
consts, invariants in a const fn that fails the BUILD. See
apps/orientation/orientation-display/src/layout.rs.

just screens is the review surface; every state should land in the gallery in both shapes.

title: Wire the IMU into the pomodoro, plant-monitor and host-monitor binaries
description:
The MPU6886 is wired into exactly one binary of four. The other three need it before they can
rotate, plus the shared rotation source spawned alongside their existing threads.

Each composition root gets the sensor on its I2C bus and the rotation source thread; the
driver, the driven adapter and the port all already exist and are shared, so this is wiring
rather than new capability.

Do host-monitor LAST and treat it as the risky one. It has WiFi plus a display thread that
already needed its stack raised to 16 KiB, and adding a periodic I2C poll to that mix is
where bus contention or a stack overflow would show up. See
kb/findings/ and the note about a network+display app's display-thread stack.

10 ms is the hard floor for any thread period (CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=100); a shorter one
busy-waits instead of yielding and starves the idle task until the watchdog fires.

Flash each one and watch serial for a reboot loop. A green host gate proves nothing here.

Open policy question this bead should settle, from the plan: whether every app SHOULD rotate
by default, or whether each binary opts in. A pomodoro timer that reflows every time you set
it down may be worse than one that stays put.
